method: After freezing the pair, reopened the programme EER package and thesis tables, the official thesis prerequisites and research seminar entry conditions. Reconstructed the 180 EC degree and tested the chronological sequence against the credit thresholds before reassessing the workbook schedules and the strongest actual historical and methodological course relationships. Read the reader-facing selections against their renderer mapping. This was a same-AI pass.
findings: The September 2026 full-time Dutch History BA comprises a 120 EC major and 60 EC profiling. Choose the first listed track and package by official order, Foundations of Europe in the History track. The major contains 60 EC of foundation courses, four 7.5 EC package courses, 7.5 EC historical writing, 7.5 EC foundations and 15 EC bachelor thesis. The 60 EC profiling includes a 30 EC minor or approved study abroad package and 30 EC free choices, with a maximum 15 EC internship. At least 15 EC of profiling is at level 2 or 3. External minors and study abroad require advance approval. The second track and other packages are valid academic directions, not components of the selected example.

Year 1 pairs a period course and methods or discipline course in each block. Its six level-1 courses supply the required 45 EC before the Foundations of Europe courses, writing and context. In Year 2 the package is taken one course per block in the order power and religion, cities, Seminar A and Seminar B. Historical Writing is in block 1 and Foundations of History in block 2. Before the two-block thesis, students earn 30 EC at level 3 and complete a qualifying Seminar A, met by the four package courses. The 30 EC advanced package plus 7.5 EC foundations and 15 EC thesis meets the major minimum of 45 EC advanced study. Profiling contributes 15 EC in Year 2 and 45 EC in Year 3 in the standard pattern.

The six level-1 first-year courses total 45 EC. The four advanced package courses total 30 EC and include Seminar A. These directly supply the checked entry thresholds. The required 15 EC thesis remains visible separately from optional UCR research.

The current workbook schedules Behavioral Economics after Research Methods & Statistics and Microeconomics & Behavior in the third option. The two other schedules retained their original feasible placements. All selections are unchanged. Researching the American Century covers source-based historical research and contributes a partial methodological comparison to Utrecht’s Seminar A. Its American focus is explicit. Renaissance Italy and World Archaeology provide concrete period material, with the medieval history course and both dedicated research seminars retaining their distinct academic content.
